by: this session, after reading all 39 agent reports and re-checking the load-bearing claims
headline: Four of the six tracks can be started this week without new wet-lab work, because the data they test against is already public. The contracting route has a parameter-free prediction and a chemistry problem.
what_was_checked_rather_than_trusted: Every citation: 217 of 221 resolve against Crossref, DataCite or arXiv AND carry the title the agent attached. 4 resolve but had no title to compare. 0 fabricated.
Every corpus entry: joined back to the bibliography fetched before any agent ran. 544 relevant of 795 read, 0 rejected, 357 of 357 quotes found verbatim in the stored abstract.
The Timoshenko ceiling the contracting route rests on: re-derived here and checked three ways (dense grid, exact rational arithmetic at the optimum, 4,000 hill-climbs that failed to beat it).
The law set: the agents were pointed at the split-out library at 1.6.0, but THIS repo carries 1.8.1. The six laws they could not see are listed under lawset_gap.

lawset_gap.problem: The law-mapping agents read fractastical/leanbio at law set 1.6.0 (53 pinned laws). This application repo is at 1.8.1 (59 pinned). Their 'existing laws' lists are short by six.
added_in_1_8_1: turing-ddi (candidate) — Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.TuringDDI.turing_instability. Directly relevant to track 2, which the agent listed as missing.
fisher-kpp-speed (candidate) — Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.KppSpeed.kpp_min_speed. Track 2 listed this as a law that would have to be formalised; it already is.
lawset_gap.also_found: 14 of the 59 pinned laws have no Lean theorem at all — they are registry placeholders with lean_ref.module = null. Among them: gene-regulatory-dynamics (track 1's target gap), fin-length-ratio, aspect-ratio-induced-drag, elastic-similarity. And 3 law files exist but are not pinned by 1.8.1: fisher-sex-ratio, hamilton-rule, turing-wavelength.

recommendation.paper: Track 3 (lumen) and track 4 (glide), run together. Both already have a result in hand from public data: the lumen agent's wild-type pilot suggests the published vertex-model sweep fails its own reproduction gate, and the glide agent ported the published blade-element model and found the published data already breaks its base-angle prediction. A paper whose first finding exists before any new data is a paper that can be written.
recommendation.contract: Track 5, but with the demonstration chosen honestly. The law gives a parameter-free prediction; stock Formlabs resins give a small, slow response. See biomaterial.the_tension.
recommendation.sequencing: Tracks 3 and 4 need no lab and no printer. Track 5 needs the printer and a week of coupon measurements before any bilayer exists. Track 1 needs only a download. Track 2 needs a 168 MB download. None of them blocks another.

tracks.verdict: Runnable now, no lab. The Cello gate libraries are public and the agent verified the raw data itself rather than trusting the scout — which changed the design, because the scout's frozen statement did not survive contact with the numbers. The claim: swapping only the ribosome binding site in front of a repressor translates the dose-response along the log-input axis, moving the threshold several-fold while leaving the Hill coefficient alone, so threshold and steepness are separable design axes.
tracks.why_it_matters: It closes a gap the registry already admits: gene-regulatory-dynamics is pinned with lean_ref.module = null. A verified invariance with a measured validity domain would be the first law in the registry about a designed circuit rather than an organism.
tracks.next: Download the Cello UCF libraries, run the calibration on Eco1C1G1T1, freeze, then score Eco1C2G2T2. The calibration maximum was 0.1587 and the frozen bound is 0.25.

tracks.verdict: Runnable now, one 168 MB download. Chemotactic range expansion in soft agar: the agent froze two zero-free-parameter predictions (the back-of-front e-fold length is u/r; bulge density goes as 1/uptake) and declared honestly which data it had already seen. It also recorded that one published square-root dependence is ALREADY refuted on the seen data — measured slope 0.30 against 0.5.
tracks.why_it_matters: turing-ddi and fisher-kpp-speed are both already in law set 1.8.1, which the agent did not know. The Lean side of this track is further along than its map says.
tracks.next: Re-run the law map against 1.8.1. Then freeze F1-F5 in one commit before adding any data module for the quarantined sheets.

tracks.verdict: Strongest paper candidate, and it already has a finding. MDCK cyst lumens: the agent ran a wild-type-only pilot and found the published vertex-model sweep gives a solidity RMSE of 0.229 against 0.124 for simply predicting the median — i.e. the published model may not reproduce wild type at all. That is a reportable result obtained from public data before any new experiment.
tracks.why_it_matters: The claim under test is that lumen shape is set by a regulated apical length per cell and cell number, NOT by pressure. Laplace pressure is already machine-checked in the library (physiology-laplace), so a refutation of the pressure picture is a refutation against a formal statement rather than a vague one.
tracks.next: Confirm the pilot by rerunning the published sweep end to end. If the reproduction gate fails, that is the paper's first figure; freeze the two held-out genotypes before touching them.

tracks.verdict: Strongest physical-build candidate, and it also already has a finding. Autorotating double-winged fruits, printable on the Formlabs machine. The agent ported the published blade-element model to Python and reproduced all five stored model files to within 0.17 %, then found the published per-trial data already fails the model's base-angle ratio: 1.50 measured against 1.22 predicted.
tracks.why_it_matters: It is the organism-scale track with a real physical comparison that does not need an organism: 21 printed fruits in a water column. The split verdict the agent predicts — the section-level model failing on base angle while the disk rule fails on pitch — would show neither law is a sufficient design constraint, and say exactly which term each lacks.
tracks.next: Print three control fruits, weigh them immersed, and run prediction G1. That single measurement decides whether the published agreement depended on an effective loading.

tracks.verdict: The law is in good shape; the materials are the problem. The Timoshenko coefficient is capped at 3/2 at a thickness ratio of n^(-1/2), so at the optimum the radius is h/(1.5 Δε) and the modulus ratio — the hardest thing to measure on a printed part — drops out of the prediction entirely. Verified here three ways. The proposed Lean theorems are in tracks/lean/HygromorphCeiling.lean.
tracks.why_it_matters: This is the pitch to an architecture practice in one line: the law names the thinnest strip that can reach a given curvature, and no material tuning beats it. It makes the design space small enough to print.
tracks.next: Print coupons and measure the swelling strain and wet modulus before any bilayer exists. Everything downstream depends on numbers nobody has published.

tracks.verdict: Reusable, and the elimination-certificate pattern is what the other five tracks should adopt: a theorem of the form *_rules_out showing a design violates a law under stated parameters. The new law set 1.8.1 adds four genuine discovery candidates. No sorry, axiom or native_decide was found anywhere in the modules the agents cited.
tracks.why_it_matters: It is the thing that makes the paper a method paper rather than four unrelated experiments: the same elimination machinery applied at four levels of organisation.
tracks.next: Write one *_rules_out certificate per track. The hygromorph one is already drafted.

biomaterial.one_line: A printed bilayer strip at the thickness ratio the law says is optimal, where the predicted radius h/(1.5 Δε) contains no fitted parameter and no modulus ratio — so the law, not a simulation, names the shape before the part exists.
biomaterial.the_law: Timoshenko bilayer curvature, already machine-checked in lean/ThompsonLaws/Hygromorphs.lean. The ceiling f ≤ 3/2 with equality at m² n = 1 is proposed in tracks/lean/HygromorphCeiling.lean and verified numerically in tracks/scripts/check-timoshenko-ceiling.py.

the_tension.problem: Stock Formlabs resins barely take up water. Every current SLA resin gains under 1 % mass in 24 h (Rigid 10K <0.1 %, Flexible 80A 0.7 %, Clear V5 0.9 %). The best stock pair is estimated at about 0.2 % differential strain in a day. And the response time goes as h²/D: at 0.4-1.6 mm with polymer diffusivities, equilibration takes days to months, not minutes.
the_tension.what_that_buys: At h = 0.8 mm and Δε = 0.2 % the predicted radius is 267 mm — a tip deflection of about 3 mm over a 40 mm strip. Measurable with a photograph and a circle fit, but not a thing you show someone across a table.
the_honest_options: SLOW AND REAL: stock resins, water or 90 % RH, measure over 7-14 days, photograph against a scale. This tests the law properly and is what the paper would use.

FAST AND LABELLED: Elastic 50A V2 gains 39 % mass in isopropanol against <0.1 % for Rigid 10K — a contrast of about 400x and a dramatic, fast demonstration. It is solvent swelling, not a humidity response, and must be labelled as such. It still tests the same law, because the law does not care how the strain arrives.
OPEN MATERIAL MODE: a PEG-acrylate hydrogel active layer against a stock passive layer gives a far larger strain, at the cost of a licence and a non-stock resin.
CAST-ON: print the passive part, then cure a thin hydrogel layer onto its green surface so the acrylate groups co-react. No tank swap, no licence.
the_tension.recommendation: Run the slow-and-real version as the test of the law, and build the solvent version as the thing to put on a table — clearly labelled, with the same geometry, so the two are visibly the same object under different stimuli.

what_nobody_has_published: A hygroscopic expansion coefficient for any Formlabs resin, or for PA11, PA12 or TPU.
A water diffusion coefficient for any Formlabs resin.
Equilibrium (not 24 h) water uptake for Formlabs resins.
Any vat-photopolymer or SLS hygromorph at all, per the hygromorph specialist's search.
A closed-form statement of the optimum m = n^(-1/2) with f = 3/2 — the physics agent derived it and could not find a source, and this session re-derived and verified it.
biomaterial.first_measurement: Print 0.5 mm and 1 mm coupons of Clear V5, Elastic 50A V2, Flexible 80A, Rigid 10K; record mass AND length at 0, 1, 3, 7, 14 days in water and at 50 % and 90 % RH. Those four numbers are the whole design space, and none of them is published.

for_the_partner.pitch: A law-constrained design pipeline: the formal law eliminates most of the design space before anything is printed, and names a number the printed part must hit. The practice gets a shape it can trust at a scale it has not built at, and a certificate saying which designs are impossible.
for_the_partner.honest_caveat: On stock printer materials the passive humidity response is small and slow. The near-term demonstration is a desk-scale object and a measurement, not a facade element.
